findings: Bilateral diffuse airspace opacification with a perihilar and mid-to-lower zone predominance, producing a bat-wing or butterfly distribution
Upper lung zones relatively spared with preserved lung lucency apically
Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged, cardiothoracic ratio appears increased
Bilateral hilar regions appear prominent and indistinct, consistent with vascular engorgement
Pulmonary vascular markings are increased and indistinct bilaterally

differential: Acute pulmonary edema (cardiogenic), given cardiomegaly and perihilar bat-wing airspace opacification
Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema / Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), given diffuse bilateral airspace disease

anatomyConcerns: Patient rotation appears minimal; projection is adequate for assessment

Cardiac enlargement should be interpreted with caution if image were AP rather than PA, however image appears consistent with PA technique

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The visible bat-wing perihilar airspace opacification with bilateral mid-to-lower zone predominance, relative upper zone sparing, and an enlarged cardiac silhouette strongly favour cardiogenic pulmonary oedema over ARDS or bilateral pneumonia. The clinical context of progressive breathlessness and ankle swelling over three months supports cardiac failure. ARDS typically lacks cardiomegaly and tends to be more diffuse without hilar predominance. Bilateral pneumonia is possible but the smooth perihilar butterfly distribution and cardiomegaly make oedema the best supported single answer. The independent read raised ARDS and pneumonia as alternatives but ranked cardiogenic oedema first; the clinical vignette resolves the tie in favour of oedema. Anatomy concerns noted by the independent read (minimal rotation, PA technique) are consistent with a genuine PA film and do not undermine the diagnosis.
